components.title: Every lab world on its first two components
components.caption: Each dot is one of the 304 lab worlds that lived to iteration 500, placed by the two directions along which the 60 statistics that do not grow with a world differ most (principal components of their standardised means over iterations 400–499). B1 10k: the thirty B1 worlds of 10,000 tokens (Experiment 2); B1 fixed: the same with brains that never change (Experiment 7); B1 100k: B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10); B1 sizes: B1 at 800 to 409,600 tokens (Experiment 8) and at 5,000 with and without a hidden layer (Experiments 12 and 13); B2 10k: the ten B2 worlds of Experiment 16; B2 var: B2 with one rule or rate changed (Experiments 9, 15 and 16); B2 5k: B2 at 5,000 tokens, with all its rules or with one taken away (Experiment 14) — except lapse: the condition in which any unused link lapses; B1 and B2 pilots: the pilot worlds that play the engine's game.
components.recipe:
**Runs.** every simulation made so far, as `book/results/worlds.json` holds it (`python3 research/atlas/across.py lab`, `pilots`, `write`): a lab run's statistics are the means of its record over a stretch of iterations; a pilot's, of 20 games recorded from its checkpoint and summarised the same way; the lab worlds that lived to iteration 500.

**Data.** From each world's means over iterations 400–499.

1. Keep the statistics that do not grow with the size of a world; divide the counts of agents (births, deaths, revolutions, leaves) by the agents.
2. Fill a missing value with the median of the worlds; standardise each statistic.
3. Take the principal components (a singular value decomposition) and draw every world on the first two.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py side_by_side`.

decided.title: What the settings decide, and what the seed does
decided.caption: Left: the share of agents that spread their stake over several nodes rather than going all in — 99% of its differences between worlds lie between conditions. Right: births per agent — under a third do; worlds of one condition differ from each other as much as the conditions do. Each dot is a world, over iterations 400–499.
